description: Coordinator hooks — session guardrails and cost optimization. REGISTRATIONS IN THIS FILE ARE READ AT SESSION START AND CACHED: adding or removing an entry here reaches NO already-running session until it runs /reload-plugins or restarts, and a deleted entry keeps firing until then. Run /reload-plugins in this session before testing your change, and expect peer sessions on this machine to keep their booted roster regardless. Hook SCRIPT bodies are unaffected — those resolve live per tool call. Measurement: docs/wiki/external-plugin-live-resolution.md § Hook REGISTRATION staleness; tripwire HOOKS-JSON-REGISTRATION-STALENESS.

SessionStart._comment: SESSIONSTART-DISPATCH FAN-IN (state/audits/2026-08-16-doe-spawn-totality-kill-list.md; state/handoffs/2026-08-16-untitled-6c1eb4ae.md § Next Steps 1) -- the single SYNC SessionStart entrypoint, replacing six of the nine standalone registrations that used to live in this array: the orientation RAM-cache injector (project-orientation.py, PM directive 2026-07-15), the settings.json integrity guard (guard-settings-integrity.py), the foreign-platform-path guard (guard-foreign-platform-paths.py), the C8 write-confinement anchor (session-start-write-bump-anchor.py), C1b EM-role assertion (assert-em-role.py), and the hook-generation self-probe (guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py). Hosting change only, never a policy change: sessionstart-dispatch.py runs all six in one interpreter, registered on the UNION of their two prior matchers (startup|clear|compact for four of them; startup|resume|clear|compact|fork for the other two -- the other two of the nine prior registrations' four distinct matcher sets, startup|compact for sweep-boot and startup alone for the commit-msg-repair hook, are not folded into this dispatcher; see below), each guard internally gated to its OWN original source set via the SessionStart payload's own `source` field (confirmed present, state/reference/anthropic-docs/claude-code/hooks.md § SessionStart) -- never a widened firing set. guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py runs LAST and every guard's captured output is flushed to real stdout/stderr IMMEDIATELY after it runs (never accumulated for one final write) because that guard's own documented fail-open path calls os._exit(0), which would otherwise silently discard an earlier guard's already-collected output — see sessionstart-dispatch.py's own module docstring for the full reasoning. NOT folded here: sweep-boot.py (own 30s-timeout registration, unchanged, immediately below — an explicit handoff instruction that its timeout must not hide behind a short one) and the two hooks that were already async:true (session-start-register-doe-claude-root.py, session-start-repair-prepare-commit-msg-hook.py — folding an async hook into this SYNC dispatcher would force it to block session start, a real behaviour change; they fold into sessionstart-async-dispatch.py instead, two entries below). Timeout 10s: the max individual folded-guard timeout was 8s (guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py); 10s gives brief sequential headroom while every folded guard is documented cheap-by-construction / near-zero-subprocess on its fast path. AMENDED 2026-08-18 -- THE 'HOSTING CHANGE ONLY, NEVER A POLICY CHANGE' CLAIM ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBES THE WHOLE ARRAY: day-branch-assert.py (chunk C4a of docs/plans/2026-08-18-enforce-day-branch-cut-tree-invariant.md) is the first genuinely git-MUTATING leg folded into this fan-in -- it cuts the day branch when the tree sits on `main`, which is a policy act, not a banner. Authorised by the PM ruling of 2026-08-18 ('we cut automatically if we're on main. we warn if we are on a branch that is not compliant with our auto-push rules'); recorded so this does not read as an undocumented contract break. It is registered `startup` ONLY and MUST STAY THAT WAY -- compact/resume/fork fire mid-execution and a cut there is the mid-execution mutation doctrine keeps out of bounds. MEASURED boot cost, correcting an earlier estimate that read `one `git branch --show-current` on the early-return path`: that estimate was wrong by an order of magnitude. On the COMPLIANT (non-`main`) path -- the overwhelmingly common one -- this guard costs 4149ms cold / ~1100ms warm and emits ZERO output, because the shim resolves the engine root, imports `coordinator_core.{hooks.day_branch_assert,machine_resolver,daily_day}`, and runs the full `assert_day_branch()` BEFORE anything establishes that the branch is already compliant. Warm split: engine import 193ms, `compute_machine()` 317ms, `assert_day_branch()` 580ms. It is 96% of this whole SYNC fan-in's cost (4149ms of 4302ms across all eight startup guards) and therefore 96% of what this array contributes to interactive boot latency. A cheap pre-gate reclaims nearly all of it without changing semantics on any non-compliant path: read `.git/HEAD` directly and return early only for a `work/*` branch with no pending-push record -- `case_b_verdict`'s own compliance definition. It does NOT consult the machine id or `local_day()`; those feed only the on-`main` cut arm (`_case_a`), which the pre-gate never reaches. Do not restore the old one-git-call claim; it was never true. The local `checkout -b` still applies on the rare lock-winner path, and the network push is still queued to the async fan-in below, deliberately kept out of this array's shared 10s budget.

SessionEnd._comment: Best-effort archival of this session's coordinator-sessions bookkeeping dir (nudge sentinels, dispatch evidence, started_at, meta.json), moved HERE from the /workstream-complete ceremony because that ceremony fires mid-session -- a session can close several workstreams before it actually ends, and archiving there reset once-per-session guards a still-live session still needed. SessionEnd fires exactly once, when the session is genuinely over. Matcher '' fires on every SessionEnd reason (clear, logout, prompt_input_exit, other) -- archival is wanted regardless of why the session ended. Shells out to the claude-klabauter-resident coordinator/bin/wsc-close.py archive-session --sid <sid> CLI (already non-fatal-by-design; see that script's own module docstring) rather than importing coordinator_core.session.scope directly, so this repo has exactly one thin caller of an entrypoint claude-klabauter already built for this call. Fails silently in every direction (unparsable stdin, absent session_id, unresolvable claude-klabauter root, subprocess timeout/failure) -- the 24h reaper is the documented backstop, so this hook must never block session teardown. Never falls back to a pid-derived or guessed session key.

SessionEnd._comment: Unattended rescue-commit+push for whatever a session left uncommitted -- fires with no invocation, for the quick-fix session too small to warrant a closure ceremony (the case /handoff's own auto-commit step never reaches, because nothing invokes it). Fails silently in every direction: a session ending is the worst moment to raise, and a commit that lands but does not push still survives.

SubagentStart._comment: C3 (docs/plans/2026-08-10-adopt-harness-native-hook-capabilities.md) -- moves the dispatched-agent bookkeeping WRITE onto SubagentStart, the first event carrying a real agent_id/agent_type identity pair, replacing the regex-scrape last resort the PostToolUse(Agent) leg used when both tool_response.agentId/.agent_id were absent. This call sends agent_id AND the real agent_type (track-dispatched-agents.py branches on hook_event_name), falling back to the literal "unknown" only when the payload carries no usable type. It formerly sent that placeholder unconditionally, so the row would land on the engine's enrich-in-place branch (coordinator_core/hooks/track_dispatched_agents.py::_resolve_row_collision) when PostToolUse(Agent) supplied type and model together. That is now inverted deliberately: PostToolUse(Agent) never fires for a Workflow agent() spawn, so the placeholder persisted permanently on exactly those rows, and the two guards keyed on column 3 failed in opposite directions off it -- the plan-body deny could not key (fail-open) while the sanctioned commit agent was refused as an unrostered type (fail-closed). Verified live: a workflow-spawned row read agent_id/unknown/unknown before this change and agent_id/unknown/coordinator:test-runner after. Cost, accepted knowingly and measured on live rows: on the RAW-AGENT-ID path the enrich call now matches on type, takes the resolver's dedup arm, and its model is dropped -- a built-in-type dispatch reading "<id> claude-sonnet-5 Explore" before this change reads "<id> unknown Explore" after; rows keyed by a named agent id are unaffected and still carry a real model. No consumer branches on that string (runtime-tripwire watchers fall through to their opus-default threshold; session-LoE undercounts opus dispatches), so it costs estimate quality, never correctness, and it closes when the engine adopts a real model onto a type-matching row. The resolver's AMBIGUOUS arm did not fire in a post-change sweep spanning coordinator:* and built-in types; on a future spelling mismatch, normalize both sides at the comparison rather than restoring the placeholder. The PostToolUse(Agent) registration below is unchanged in shape; it still writes, now purely as the enrichment call. Column 4 (timestamp) is deliberately set here, nearer the true dispatch moment, and preserved by the enrich branch rather than overwritten. Failure mode (Review: coordinator:code-reviewer, Finding 5): if the PostToolUse(Agent) enrich fire never lands for a given agent (state/bug-backlog/2026-08-10-posttooluse-agent-does-not-fire-for-some-8c1d40be9f2a.yaml documents this happens), this create call's placeholder row -- subagent_type="unknown", dispatched_model="unknown" -- now persists PERMANENTLY instead of the dispatch going unrecorded as it did pre-C3. Accepted tradeoff: a permanently-unknown row beats a dispatch recorded nowhere, but it means a future reader diagnosing stale "unknown" rows in dispatched-agents.txt cannot distinguish 'genuinely unresolved' from 'enrich never fired' without checking the linked bug. THE SHIM NOW CARRIES TWO OPS via dispatch_ops_from_hook: the bookkeeping op above runs FIRST, then the catering op, because the catering op reads back through dispatched-agents.txt and needs the bookkeeping write already landed. Catering moved here from PreToolUse(Agent) because that event has no agent_id and never fires for a Workflow agent() spawn. This is deliberately NOT a second SubagentStart entry: a second entry would price a second permanent python3 cold start (~642ms fleet-wide) against DR-344's 500ms brightline -- riding the existing shim avoids that.

SubagentStop._comment: Stage 1 of the mechanical zero-tool-use subagent detector (docs/plans/2026-07-25-zero-tool-use-detection.md, C1/C2) -- fires on every subagent completion, reads the payload's agent_transcript_path (never the decoy transcript_path -- see the plan's AC10/Pinned contract), and relays to the coordinator_core.hooks.subagent_zero_tool_use claude-klabauter op, which counts tool_use blocks and writes the durable detection record. It relays a SECOND op in the same in-process dispatch_ops_from_hook call -- coordinator_core.hooks.subagent_review_mark, which derives a commit-ledger review mark from a finishing reviewer's own reviewed_range findings. That op is deliberately NOT a second SubagentStop entry in this file: a second entry would buy a second permanent python3 cold start (the ~642ms priced below) on every subagent stop fleet-wide, where folding it into this entry's existing call adds no process at all. Per-op errors are returned by that seam rather than raised, so neither op can suppress the other -- which is what makes it safe for the review-mark op to be registered here while a published engine mirror predating it still resolves the method to a returned error. Emits nothing (DEC-4: a SubagentStop hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext reaches only the subagent's own context, never the EM's -- Stage 2, folded into the existing UserPromptSubmit runtime-tripwire-em-check.py entry below, is what surfaces it). Registered LAST, only after the claude-klabauter op landed (claude-klabauter commit 82224422) -- an unregistered script is inert; a registered one that silently no-ops on every SubagentStop until the op exists is the exact fail-open-reads-as-healthy shape this workstream exists to kill. This registration percolates to every OSS install of the coordinator plugin, most of which have no claude-klabauter and therefore no engine op to resolve -- for those installs this is a permanent per-SubagentStop python3 cold start (~642ms on the reference Windows machine) that can only ever no-op, same as the other _engine_root-gated entries in this file; precedented, not a blocker, but named here rather than shipped silently.

UserPromptExpansion._comment: handoff residue-segment retrieval seam (third UserPromptExpansion entry). Fires on a `handoff` verb invocation (same bare-verb-vs-namespaced normalization as pickup-autofire.py/mise-autofire.py); computes the active case set for coordinator/skills/handoff/residue/'s segment contract (`shared` unconditionally, `dirty-tree` from a read-only `git status --porcelain`, `predecessor`/`carried-items` from the read-only `baton-assemble brief handoff` CLI, self-resolving to this session's own held handoff claim), selects every segment whose `case` is active, sorts ascending by `order`, and injects the concatenated bodies as additionalContext -- so the EM never hand-opens a segment file. Read-only end to end: `apply` is never invoked from this hook and there is no mutating half. async:false because the segment set must land in the SAME turn the EM's /handoff prompt is being expanded into. Every failure mode (unresolvable baton-assemble binary, non-zero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, missing/unreadable residue directory, a single malformed segment) degrades to silent pass -- this hook never blocks /handoff, which fires under context pressure by definition. Budget-capped (see `_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS` in the script's own module docstring for the exact figure -- deliberately NOT the 10,000 chars pickup-autofire.py/mise-autofire.py carry), degrading class:droppable segments before ever touching a class:protected one. Install-surface note: this hook type required /reload-plugins to start firing during the spike that proved the mechanism (see pickup-autofire.py's own module docstring for the same finding) -- a plain hooks.json edit alone was not observed to be enough on its own.

Timeout stays 15s: both folded guards are cheap string/regex work (no filesystem stat, no subprocess) that adds low-single-digit ms to the all-miss path, well inside the existing 15s ceiling sized for the engine leg's own worst case. Strips isolation: "worktree" out of a Workflow dispatch's tool_input before the call proceeds -- design-as-offers: the dispatch SUCCEEDS without the worktree rather than being denied and forcing a full retry. isolation: "remote" and every other value pass through untouched. Single-emitter fix (2026-07-31): this used to be registered on matcher Agent|Workflow, racing enforce-agent-dispatch-mode.py's own updatedInput emission on the SAME Agent tool call (same-event PreToolUse hooks run in parallel with undefined completion order; updatedInput is last-writer-wins) -- confirmed live on harness 2.1.220. Narrowed to Workflow only; Agent's worktree-isolation strip now lives inside enforce-agent-dispatch-mode.py (the sole updatedInput emitter for Agent), sharing this script's strip computation via the new _worktree_isolation_strip.py module rather than duplicating it. See coordinator/hooks/scripts/strip-worktree-isolation.py module docstring for the full rationale and the shared .coordinator-override-worktree-guard sentinel.

PreToolUse._comment: PREUSE-WRITE-DISPATCH — the single PreToolUse(Write|Edit|MultiEdit) entrypoint (docs/plans/2026-08-06-hook-spawn-fan-in-finish-and-extend.md § C4, fan-in AC-1). Resolves the claude-klabauter engine in-process, then batches EVERY guard enrolled on `_guard_runner.REAL_GUARD_REGISTRY` for this matcher — currently 51, of which only 8 are DoE-resident (`scripts/`) and 43 live in the ENGINE plane (`write_guards/`, claude-klabauter). READ `x-effective-delivery.carriers` FOR THE LIVE SET, NEVER THIS COMMENT: an earlier version of this line named five DoE scripts, which sent a 2026-08-15 investigation grepping this repo for a deny that `bump_out_of_repo_tool_write` had raised from claude-klabauter. A count in prose goes stale silently; the carrier block is generated into the SAME interpreter via the in-process guard runner (coordinator/hooks/scripts/_guard_runner.py), each guard's own two-stage lazy-import scope descriptor deciding whether it is even imported for a given write. Class-aware aggregation (_guard_runner_contract.py clause 10): at most one deny reaches the harness, but a deny from one guard and an advisory from another on the SAME write both surface. This rewiring moves WHERE guards run, never what they decide — each guard's own module docstring still states its policy.

PreToolUse._comment: BLOCK-WORKTREE-TOOL — structural git-worktree ban, one leg of a multi-leg campaign. Denies EnterWorktree unconditionally (worktrees degrade on Windows and don't scale to concurrent-agent dispatch; the sanctioned shape is scoped-parallel dispatch into the same tree). ExitWorktree always ALLOWED — leaving a worktree is cleanup, never blocked, or an agent already inside one gets trapped. Override: repo-root sentinel file ONLY (no env-var leg — a subagent can set an env var on itself, defeating an env-var override for a guard that must bind subagents too). Deny message deliberately never names the sentinel file.

PostToolUse._comment: POSTUSE-STOP-FAMILY-DISPATCH — the combined PostToolUse entrypoint (docs/plans/2026-08-06-hook-spawn-fan-in-finish-and-extend.md § C4b) for the four Stop-family write-path advisory guards (derive-global-doctrine-live-copy, derive-setup-copies, nudge-initiative-goals-ladder, nudge-new-file-zero-budget-ratchets — formerly four standalone registrations on this matcher, now `_stop_family_runner.REAL_STOP_FAMILY_REGISTRY`). Each guard writes its own advisory directly to stderr and returns exit 2 (the Stop-family protocol, distinct from the PreToolUse deny/additionalContext envelope shape `preuse-write-dispatch.py` uses); this dispatcher batches all four into ONE process via the in-process Stop-family runner (coordinator/hooks/scripts/_stop_family_runner.py), aggregating via CONCATENATE-ALL (never first-fires-wins — every guard that fires on a payload has its text reach the combined stderr, and the combined exit code is 2 if any fired). See coordinator/hooks/scripts/_stop_family_runner_contract.py for why this is a SIBLING mechanism to _guard_runner.py, not an extension of it. Policy byte-identical — this moves WHERE these guards run, never what they decide.

PostToolUse._comment: Phase 3 consolidation (docs/plans/2026-06-30-pretooluse-bash-hook-dispatcher.md), RE-SCOPED off matcher "" 2026-08-16 (state/handoffs/2026-08-16-untitled-6c1eb4ae.md Next Steps 1, third bullet; state/audits/2026-08-16-doe-spawn-totality-kill-list.md K-01). DIVERGENCE FROM THE HANDOFF'S LITERAL 'move the advisory to Stop': verified two of the four folded checks (the once-per-session first-Agent-dispatch sidecar advisory, gated tool_name=="Agent"; the unauthorized-handoff nudge, gated tool_name=="Write"+file_path/content) read fields a Stop payload never carries -- moving the whole bundle to Stop would silently and permanently disable both, since their own internal tool_name gates would never match again. Narrowed the matcher instead, to exactly the tool set the four checks' own internal gates need (Agent for the first-dispatch advisory, Write for the handoff nudge, all four write-tools for the folded track_touched_files call below) rather than moving event. Context-pressure and runtime-tripwire (the two truly tool_name-agnostic checks) still fire on this narrower set rather than literally every tool call -- both are throttle/bark-once gated, so this loses at most a few minutes of latency in a session with a long non-write/non-Agent stretch, never a suppression. This is a command spawn (not an mcp_tool). The script merges the four checks' additionalContext into a single emission (see postuse-advisory-dispatch.py). timeout 10 preserves the former per-hook budget headroom.
